rows.learner_decision: When heart failure is a plausible cause of dyspnea, select an ECG and chest radiograph and use natriuretic peptide testing and echocardiography to support or refute the diagnosis rather than relying on one finding alone.
load_bearing_propositions: No single symptom, sign, or test establishes heart failure in a patient with dyspnea; ECG, chest radiography, natriuretic peptides, and echocardiography have complementary diagnostic roles.

sources.title: 2017 Comprehensive Update of the Canadian Cardiovascular Society Guidelines for the Management of Heart Failure
sources.locator: Diagnosis of HF and Biomarkers/NPs sections
sources.support_summary: The guideline combines clinical assessment with ECG, chest radiography, natriuretic peptides, and echocardiography and cautions against a single-test diagnosis.

rows.learner_decision: Before prescribing a medication with interaction risk, reconcile prescription, non-prescription, natural-health, and food exposures and verify clinically important drug-drug and drug-food interactions in the current Canadian product monograph.
load_bearing_propositions: Medication-interaction assessment requires a complete exposure history and consultation of current Canadian product-monograph interaction sections.

sources.title: Guidance Document: Product Monograph
sources.support_summary: The monograph framework identifies dedicated drug-drug and drug-food interaction sections for current prescribing decisions.

rows.learner_decision: Recognize dermatophyte infection from its site and morphology and use microscopy or culture when the diagnosis is uncertain or nail disease requires organism differentiation.
load_bearing_propositions: Dermatophyte syndromes are distinguished by site and morphology; microscopy or culture is useful when the diagnosis is uncertain and culture helps distinguish causes of nail disease.

sources.title: Antifungal agents for common outpatient paediatric infections
sources.locator: Tinea corporis; Tinea pedis and onychomycosis
sources.support_summary: The practice point describes site-specific tinea morphology and the role of microscopy or culture when uncertainty or nail disease is present.

rows.learner_decision: For a child at least two years old with suspected celiac disease, order tTG-IgA with total IgA while the child is eating gluten and refer a positive screen for specialist confirmation before starting a gluten-free diet.
load_bearing_propositions: Initial testing for suspected celiac disease at age two or older uses tTG-IgA with total IgA on a gluten-containing diet; a positive screen requires confirmation and a gluten-free diet should not begin before diagnostic testing.

sources.title: Celiac Disease: Diagnosis and Management
sources.support_summary: The Canadian professional resource recommends tTG-IgA first for age two and older, adequate gluten intake, total IgA assessment, and biopsy-based confirmation after a positive screen.

rows.learner_decision: When measles is suspected in a febrile child with compatible respiratory symptoms and rash, institute airborne isolation immediately and report the suspected case to the local public health authority while confirmatory testing is arranged.
load_bearing_propositions: Measles is airborne; suspected cases require immediate isolation and health professionals must report suspected cases to local public health.

sources.title: Measles: For health professionals
sources.support_summary: PHAC directs health professionals to suspect compatible presentations, report suspected cases locally, and use airborne precautions; suspect cases isolate while testing is pending.

rows.learner_decision: Measure TSB or TcB without delay in a newborn with clinically apparent jaundice and interpret the result against age-in-hours, gestational age, and neurotoxicity-risk thresholds to decide on treatment and follow-up.
load_bearing_propositions: Visible or suspected significant neonatal jaundice requires prompt bilirubin measurement; treatment and follow-up depend on an hour-specific threshold modified by gestational age and neurotoxicity risk.

sources.title: Guidelines for detection and management of hyperbilirubinemia in term and late preterm newborns
sources.locator: Clinical assessment; bilirubin measurement; treatment thresholds
sources.support_summary: CPS requires prompt TSB or TcB for suspected significant jaundice and bases management on age-specific thresholds and neurotoxicity risk.

rows.learner_decision: In a patient with symptomatic vaginal discharge, use the history, examination, vaginal pH and indicated microscopy or molecular testing to distinguish bacterial vaginosis, vulvovaginal candidiasis, and trichomoniasis before selecting organism-specific treatment.
load_bearing_propositions: Bacterial vaginosis, vulvovaginal candidiasis, and trichomoniasis are common infectious causes of vaginal discharge and should be differentiated with clinical and laboratory findings before targeted management.

sources.title: STI-associated syndromes guide: Vaginitis
sources.support_summary: The Canadian guide identifies the common infectious causes and provides clinical-manifestation and diagnostic-testing pathways before management.

rows.learner_decision: Confirm suspected PMS or PMDD with prospective daily symptom charting across menstrual cycles and distinguish it from continuous psychiatric symptoms or premenstrual exacerbation before initiating syndrome-specific treatment.
load_bearing_propositions: Prospective daily symptom charting is required to establish cyclical timing and distinguish PMS or PMDD from situational disorders and premenstrual exacerbation of another disorder.

sources.title: Premenstrual syndrome and premenstrual dysphoric disorder: guidelines for management
sources.support_summary: The Canadian hospital guideline uses daily symptom charting to distinguish PMS and PMDD from situational illness and premenstrual exacerbation.
sources.currentness_limit: Older guideline; used only for stable diagnostic timing, not drug dosing.

rows.learner_decision: At the initial prenatal visit, obtain baseline CBC, blood group and antibody screen, rubella immunity, syphilis, hepatitis B and HIV testing, and arrange additional infection and genetic screening according to jurisdiction and individual risk.
load_bearing_propositions: The initial prenatal assessment includes specified baseline blood and infection screening, with other tests determined by provincial guidance and patient risk.

sources.title: Care during pregnancy: Family-centred maternity and newborn care national guidelines
sources.locator: Initial visit and Appendix B laboratory screening
sources.support_summary: The national guideline lists first-visit clinical and laboratory assessment and notes jurisdiction-specific prenatal screening schedules.

rows.learner_decision: Treat suspected esophageal perforation as a surgical emergency: stop oral intake, begin broad-spectrum antimicrobial and resuscitative therapy, obtain urgent specialist source-control assessment, and avoid delaying operative management when indicated.
load_bearing_propositions: Suspected esophageal perforation requires NPO status, broad-spectrum antibiotics, resuscitation, and urgent source-control assessment; delayed indicated surgery worsens outcomes.

sources.title: Esophageal emergencies: WSES guidelines
sources.locator: Esophageal perforation non-operative and surgical management
sources.support_summary: The guideline requires NPO, broad-spectrum aerobic and anaerobic coverage and urgent source control, with prompt surgery when indicated.
sources.fallback_reason: No suitable current Canadian national or specialty guideline was found in the bounded search.

rows.learner_decision: Initiate antibiotics and supportive care for acute cholecystitis and select early laparoscopic cholecystectomy for a suitable patient with mild disease, modifying source control according to severity and operative risk.
load_bearing_propositions: Canadian acute-care guidance recommends antibiotics and supportive care initially and includes early laparoscopic cholecystectomy for suitable mild acute cholecystitis, with other approaches for greater severity or risk.

sources.title: Dynamic Practice Guidelines for Emergency General Surgery: Biliary Colic and Cholecystitis
sources.support_summary: The CAGS handbook lists antibiotics and supportive care and early laparoscopic cholecystectomy for mild disease, with severity-dependent alternatives.

rows.learner_decision: Recognize acute painless monocular vision loss from suspected retinal arterial ischemia as a stroke-equivalent emergency and arrange immediate stroke-centre assessment rather than routine outpatient ophthalmology follow-up.
load_bearing_propositions: Retinal ischemic injury is an ischemic stroke; acute symptomatic retinal artery occlusion warrants immediate stroke-centre referral for systemic evaluation and possible acute intervention.

sources.title: Definitions
sources.support_summary: Canadian Stroke Best Practices includes retinal cell death from ischemia within the definition of ischemic stroke.

sources.title: Retinal and Ophthalmic Artery Occlusions
sources.support_summary: The specialty guideline directs immediate referral of acute symptomatic retinal arterial occlusion to the nearest stroke referral centre.
sources.fallback_reason: The Canadian source establishes stroke equivalence but did not provide the retinal-occlusion-specific referral sentence.

rows.learner_decision: Diagnose schizoaffective disorder when a mood episode occurs with schizophrenia-spectrum psychosis, mood symptoms occupy a substantial portion of the illness, and psychosis has persisted for at least two weeks without prominent mood symptoms.
load_bearing_propositions: Schizoaffective disorder requires concurrent mood and psychotic symptoms plus at least two weeks of psychosis without prominent mood symptoms, with mood symptoms present for a substantial illness duration.

sources.organization: Centre for Addiction and Mental Health
sources.title: Psychosis: Diagnosis
sources.support_summary: CAMH states the concurrent mood/psychosis pattern, substantial mood-duration requirement, and two-week psychosis-without-prominent-mood criterion.

rows.learner_decision: Offer CBT for generalized anxiety disorder and, when medication is indicated, use an SSRI or SNRI as first-line pharmacotherapy rather than long-term benzodiazepine treatment.
load_bearing_propositions: CBT is a first-choice psychological treatment for anxiety disorders; SSRIs and SNRIs are effective first-line pharmacotherapy for GAD, while benzodiazepines should be brief because of dependence risk.

sources.organization: Centre for Addiction and Mental Health
sources.title: Anxiety: Pharmacotherapy
sources.support_summary: CAMH identifies SSRI/SNRI options as first-line for GAD and limits benzodiazepines to brief use; its 2024 guide identifies CBT as first-choice psychotherapy.

rows.learner_decision: Diagnose a substance use disorder when at least two of eleven DSM-5 criteria occur within twelve months and grade severity as mild with two or three, moderate with four or five, and severe with six or more criteria.
load_bearing_propositions: A substance use disorder requires at least two of eleven criteria within twelve months; severity is mild at two to three, moderate at four to five, and severe at six or more.

sources.organization: Canadian Centre on Substance Use and Addiction
sources.title: Improving Quality of Life: Substance Use and Aging
sources.support_summary: The Canadian report states the two-of-eleven threshold, twelve-month window, and mild, moderate, and severe criterion counts.

rows.learner_decision: Use the Health Belief Model to identify whether perceived susceptibility and severity, expected benefit, or perceived barriers are limiting a patient's preventive-health behaviour and tailor counselling to the limiting construct.
load_bearing_propositions: The Health Belief Model links preventive action to perceived susceptibility and severity, perceived effectiveness or benefit, and psychological, financial, or other barriers.

sources.organization: Association of Faculties of Medicine of Canada
sources.title: AFMC Primer on Population Health: Chapter 2
sources.support_summary: The AFMC primer defines preventive action through perceived susceptibility and severity, expected benefit, and barriers or costs.

rows.learner_decision: Recognize that a negligence claim in a common-law Canadian jurisdiction requires duty of care, breach of the reasonable standard of care, patient harm, and a causal connection between the breach and harm; an adverse outcome alone is insufficient.
load_bearing_propositions: Medical negligence in common-law Canada requires duty, breach, harm, and causation, and the standard is reasonable care rather than perfection.

sources.title: Medico-legal handbook for physicians in Canada
sources.locator: Negligence, civil responsibility, and the standard of care
sources.support_summary: The CMPA handbook lists duty, breach, harm, and causation and distinguishes reasonable professional care from a guarantee of a good outcome.
sources.jurisdiction_limit: Common-law provinces and territories; Quebec civil responsibility is analogous but legally distinct.

rows.learner_decision: Identify random allocation to intervention and control groups as the design feature that best balances measured and unmeasured confounders, while recognizing that blinding instead reduces expectation-related measurement bias.
load_bearing_propositions: Random allocation is the most attractive design-stage control for confounding because it tends to balance characteristics; blinding addresses participant and assessor expectation bias rather than confounding.

sources.organization: Association of Faculties of Medicine of Canada
sources.title: AFMC Primer on Population Health: Chapter 5
sources.locator: Randomized controlled trials; dealing with confounding
sources.support_summary: The AFMC primer explains random allocation as the strongest design-stage control for confounding and blinding as protection against expectation-driven outcome assessment bias.
